title: 新游汇总：SuperPlay 与 Playtika 的下一批游戏、任天堂新应用、Spirit Crossing 等
content:
New game digest: SuperPlay and Playtika’s next games, new Nintendo apps, Spirit Crossing, more – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
Here every Friday you’ll find the latest global releases, game dates, new soft launches and everything in between.
This column is sponsored by
exmox
.

.
Disney Merge Dreams (SuperPlay/Playtika)
Disney Solitaire maker SuperPlay, which
Playtika bought in 2024
, has put Disney Merge Dreams into soft launch on
iOS
in Colombia and the Philippines. It’s also live on
Google Play
, where it has passed 1,000 downloads.
AppMagic first spotted the iOS version on November 17. It’s a merge game inspired by Disney Parks, featuring Disney and Pixar characters including Cinderella and Stitch.
Bingo Gees (Playtika)
Playtika has soft launched this new bingo game on Android only in the Philippines, according to
AppMagic
.
Hello Peach and Hello Luigi (Nintendo)
Nintendo has quietly added two more free kids apps to its My Mario line-up. Hello Peach and Hello Luigi arrived on Google Play in October and on iOS on November 10,
according to AppMagic
.
They follow
Hello Mario
, which launched in August 2025. Downloads are modest so far, with around 16,700 for Hello Peach and 11,100 for Hello Luigi across both stores.
Spirit Crossing (Spry Fox)
First announced as a Netflix game, social MMO
Spirit Crossing
is now out on iOS, PC, Switch and Switch 2.
Cozy Grove developer Spry Fox took it along when it went independent from Netflix last December. It costs $29.99 on PC and Switch, and there’s an optional Cozy Club subscription on top.
Everything Is Crab (Secret Mode)
This cheerful indie game is coming to iOS and Android next week, on November 24. It’s looking like a free-to-start game, but the price to unlock the full game has not yet been confirmed.
Clone Drone in the Danger Zone (Doborog Games)
After a decade on PC and console, Doborog’s robot-slicing action game
arrived on iOS and Android
on November 13, alongside a 10th anniversary update.
The studio says it has sold more than 2 million copies, and it has 97% positive reviews from 36,300 players on Steam.
Hillthorn (Raw Fury)
There’s no dialogue in
Hillthorn
, the card-based investigation game from Raw Fury and Montreal’s Fool Moon. Players piece together the search for a missing child using only Clue cards.
It launched on iOS, Android, PC and Switch on November 10.
Top Guilds (Phantom Gamelabs)
Phantom Gamelabs has soft launched its casual action RPG with a social twist. It’s available on iOS and Android in the US, Japan, South Korea, Finland, the Philippines and Thailand.
Scrabble Shake-Up and Scattergories Party (Netflix)
Two party games joined Netflix’s Games on TV on November 17. Scrabble Shake-Up has everyone playing at the same time, while in Scattergories Party players shout out words that match a category against the clock.
They sit alongside Netflix Minigolf, Unhinged and Boggle Party in the TV line-up, which uses phones as controllers.
World War II: TCG (Games for a Living)
Strategy card game World War II: TCG is
returning
after four years offline, with an open beta on iOS and Android starting
November 28.
Originally released in 2014, it was pulled from stores in 2022 when its backend service shut down. Web3 company Games for a Living now runs it and plans to add card trading on its marketplace after the beta, although players won’t need a crypto wallet to play.
Papgame (Not Just Music)
Based on the Italian animated film Papmusic – Animation for Fashion,
Papgame
is open for pre-registration on Google Play, with iOS to follow.
Developer Not Just Music has split it into two modes. Papcrazy is a first-person adventure in Milan’s Piazza Duomo, where players throw hearts at characters to make them dance, and Paprhythm is a rhythm game. Around 50 songs will be available at launch.
Blood Line: A Rebel Moon Game (Netflix)
Netflix is pulling the plug on Blood Line: A Rebel Moon Game on December 9, less than 17 months after it launched on iOS and Android in July 2025,
What’s on Netflix reports
.
The online-only co-op action game was made by Vainglory studio Super Evil Megacorp and is based on Zack Snyder’s Rebel Moon films. Because it was a Netflix exclusive built on Netflix’s own IP, it has nowhere else to go once the servers are switched off.
